svg.title: Figure 1. Test set-up
svg.desc: Three panels. (a) The strut frame: a bar stands vertically between two knife edges seated in V-blocks, the upper one under a loading screw in the crosshead and the lower one on a load cell. The bar is drawn bowed to the right (exaggerated). The load P acts downward at the top end A; B is the bottom end; L is the distance between the pivots. A dial gage touches the bar at mid-length on the right (convex, front) side, and strain gages are bonded at mid-length on the front and back faces. Beer's axes are shown: x pointing down the column from A and y pointing to the right. (b) The end fixtures: a knife-edge holder with three V-grooves at offsets of 0, 1 and 2 mm from the axis, used for Parts A and C, and a clamp block that grips 40 mm of the bar between two jaws, used for Part B and Part D. (c) The 25.4 by 6.35 mm cross-section seen along the column: it bends across the 6.35 mm thickness t, in the y direction, with the front gage F on the convex face and the back gage B on the opposite face; the radius of gyration is t over the square root of 12.
